headline: Cabinet Division bans PM Tarique's photo on govt event displays
summary: A new directive prohibits the use of the Prime Minister's image on banners, festoons, and billboards for government programs, prioritizing event themes instead.
details: The Cabinet Division has banned the use of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's photograph on banners, festoons, and billboards prepared for government events.
The directive was issued in a circular signed by Cabinet Division Deputy Secretary Tania Afroz and takes effect immediately.
According to the circular, the Prime Minister's photo cannot be used in 3D or any other form on these displays.
The directive mandates that the subject of the event must be given priority in the design of banners and billboards.
Only necessary and relevant information should be included, ensuring the design clearly reflects the objective, message, and theme of the event.
caption:
No more PM photos on government banners. The Cabinet Division has issued a strict new directive.

The Cabinet Division has banned the use of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's photograph on banners, festoons, and billboards prepared for government events.

The directive was issued in a circular signed by Cabinet Division Deputy Secretary Tania Afroz and takes effect immediately.

According to the circular, the Prime Minister's photo cannot be used in 3D or any other form on these displays.

The directive mandates that the subject of the event must be given priority in the design of banners and billboards.

Only necessary and relevant information should be included, ensuring the design clearly reflects the objective, message, and theme of the event.

Source: Jamuna TV, Somoy News, The Daily Star

headline_marked: 438 killed in June: [[One in three road accident victims was a motorcyclist]]
headline: 438 killed in June: One in three road accident victims was a motorcyclist
summary: A Road Safety Foundation report reveals 472 accidents in June, with motorcyclists and pedestrians facing the highest risks.
details: In June, 438 people were killed and 561 injured in 472 road accidents across Bangladesh, according to the Road Safety Foundation.
The report highlights a alarming trend: 134 of the deceased were motorcyclists, accounting for approximately 31% of the total deaths.
Pedestrians were also highly vulnerable, with 91 people losing their lives. Among the dead were 44 women and 56 children.
Regional roads saw the highest number of accidents with 194 cases, followed by national highways (151), rural roads (64), and city roads (57).
Loss of vehicle control was the primary cause of accidents (206 cases), followed by head-on collisions (109) and hitting pedestrians (97).
The Dhaka division recorded the highest number of accidents with 116 cases and 118 deaths, while Mymensingh had the fewest with 19 accidents and 16 deaths.
The Road Safety Foundation attributed these crashes to faulty vehicles, reckless speed, driver inefficiency, and poor traffic management.
The organization has proposed a 12-point recommendation, including reforming the BRTA, removing expired vehicles, and increasing public awareness.
